correctness.rationale: Independently checked the graph-maturity induction from K_pq (p,q>=3): add edge within one original part, subdivide it to introduce a third-part vertex, add all incident missing first/second-part edges; deletion of endpoints leaves a connected existing complete bipartite core. Farber–Hanbury Theorem 1 and Proposition 22 verify premises. Reconstructed 0/1/2-cell types of unordered two-point deleted-product cubical complex and signed permutations, including -1 for swapped edge-pair cells; first H1 module is H1(G). Symbolic exact expansion of the virtual Euler character and Specht characters f_i,t_i simplifies identically to proposed closed formula; dimensions checked at (3,3,3),(3,3,4),(3,4,4),(4,4,4) as 81,146,252,414. Multiplicities nonnegative; semisimplicity gives rational isomorphism. Finite examples corroborate the all-parameter character identity rather than proving it.

originality.rationale: Farber–Hanbury 2010 proves maturity/bipartite Betti formulas but does not give the three-independent-factor S_p×S_q×S_r H2 representation. Ramos–He Yun 2026 Theorems 3.30/3.31 concern two large parts and a singleton, with only diagonal S_n action (its graph even deletes corresponding matching edges), so neither object nor group action dominates the present theorem. The full 34-constituent Specht formula and fixed/2-cycle character are not entailed by those prior statements.
residual_risks: A different equivariant theorem for the same full three-part family, perhaps under FI^3 terminology, could be missed.
The proof depends on correct equivariant maturity; verified exact edge-addition hypothesis and base but did not reproduce the original topological proof.
No integral splitting or torsion-freeness is established for arbitrary p,q,r.
